answer: Persistent work history as collateral. Each agent identity accrues a signed record of completed tasks, and rewards are released only against that record. Cloning resets the record, so a fresh identity must redo low-value work before earning anything. The protocol treats this history as the kernel of trust, weighting payouts by verified tenure. An attacker cloning N identities pays N times the ramp-up labor, plus a copper-level fee per new record write, making honest continuation cheaper than duplication. Honest agents keep one dune of accumulated history while clones start at zero.
